text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - Leading British blue chips lost ground on Wednesday after a surprisingly strong employment report reignited fears of an interest rate hike. A sharp drop on Wall Street also spooked investors who had watched U.S. shares reach record highs no less than four times this year. The FTSE 100 ended 9.3 points lower at 4,158.9.
FRANKFURT - A strongly bullish tone reigned on the German stock market on Wednesday, sending the blue chip DAX index to fresh all-time highs.

Spurred on by a global markets boom, Tuesday's benign U.S. consumer prices report and the dollar's continued rally, the DAX gained 39.57 points, or 1.3 percent, to end the floor session at 2,988.45 -- a record close. In post-bourse trade the index down 2.28 to 2,976.56.
PARIS - Profit-taking in the afternoon brought French shares to a softer close. Traders said a consolidation was natural after yesterday's rapid rise to historic highs.
Traders cited various factors supporting the orderly retreat, including health worries for Russian President Boris Yeltsin and weakness on Wall Street and in U.S. Treasuries.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 14.16 points or 0.59 percent at 2,387.98. The CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,391 from 2,406 on Tuesday's close.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended lower despite early record highs above 4,000 points on the Swiss Market Index (SMI) after profit-taking in heavyweights Novartis and Nestle led the market down. The SMI ended down 4.0 points, or 0.1 percent, at 3,979.67 points after hitting an all-time high of 4,004.8 points in early trade. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) fell 3.66 points, or 0.14 percent, to 2,551.75. TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market was closed on Wednesday for a national holiday. Trade will resume on Thursday.
On Tuesday, the Nikkei 225 closed 25.66 points or 0.14 percent lower at 18,093.13, rescued from an earlier plunge of over 500 points by buying interest in blue-chip issues.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index stormed to record highs on Wednesday, as banking and property stocks shot up on expectations of a slew of warrant issues and after U.S. economic data soothed interest rate jitters.
The blue-chip index surged 472.78 points, or 3.56 percent, to a record close of 13,766.65, after hitting a record intra-day high of 13,771.54.
SYDNEY - The Australian share market stormed to a record close on Wednesday after U.S. markets rallied on consumer price data that eased U.S. inflation concerns.

The market set sail higher right from the opening bell and by midsession was cruising in uncharted waters, reaching a record intraday high of 2,444.2. This surpasssed the previous record high of 2,438.8, set on January 10, 1997.
The All Ordinaries index jumped 18.8 points to 2,438.2 by the close, surpassing the previous record close of 2424.6, set on December 31.

JOHANNESBURG - The weak bullion price -- failing to sustain its brief attempt at a rally and fixing at a 3-1/4 year low in London -- hammered away at South African gold stocks on Wednesday, dragging them lower but failing to force them to finish at the day's worst levels. Industrials enjoyed a healthy day but finished off their best levels on profit-taking with Mandela's rebuff of the U.S. warning on the Syrian arms deal taking the shine off performance.
Golds lost 41.5 points to 1,408.4, industrials added 4.9 to 8,130.7 and all-shares dipped 0.1 to 6,751.4.
